The 2020 George Floyd protests were a broad wave of demonstrations against police violence and racial injustice, sparked by the killing of George Floyd in Minneapolis.

On May 25, 2020, Floyd, a Black man, died after Minneapolis police officer Derek Chauvin knelt on his neck for more than nine minutes during an arrest. Video of the encounter spread widely, prompting protests in Minneapolis and then across the United States and around the world. The demonstrations took place amid the COVID-19 pandemic and drew on longstanding concerns about police treatment of Black people, including the earlier killings of Breonna Taylor and Ahmaud Arbery.

Many protests were peaceful, with marches, vigils, and calls for accountability and changes to policing. Some areas also saw clashes with police, fires, looting, and property damage. Police and other authorities used measures including curfews, arrests, tear gas, and other crowd-control tactics; those responses became a subject of further criticism and debate.

The movement helped make “Black Lives Matter” a central slogan in public discussion and renewed calls for reforms such as greater police accountability, changes to use-of-force rules, and investment in communities. The protests also prompted disputes over public safety, policing, and the movement’s proposals. Chauvin was later convicted of Floyd’s murder, while debate over broader changes to policing continued.
